The assignment ignores the status of the request and the assignments it already has: a cancelled, expired or filled request accepts more assignments and has its status rewritten, the same member can be offered twice, and filled is derived from the length of the one posted list.

The seniority, rotation, availability and skills ranking and the organization rules table exist, but no route calls the ranking and no route writes a rule, so the assignment is whatever member list the officer posts and the fairness the hall model describes is not applied.
When the stats query fails the route logs the error and answers 200 with every count at zero, so a database failure reads on the dashboard as an organization with no claims and no members.

The leadership compliance metrics report deadline adherence and documentation rate as 100 when there are no alerts, and nothing writes alerts; the grievance aggregates silently stop at the first five thousand rows and the alerts at one thousand; the figures are cached per organization.

The CSV export is guarded by authentication alone, with no organization, role or entitlement, and its data source is not wired: production answers 501, every other environment answers 200 with an empty file; once wired the case export would carry case ids, assignees and worksites with no organization predicate in the route.

The enterprise data subject request route is the generic factory over a subject-owned table with no owner column, so every read and write is refused with a 403 that names a dedicated route, and the dedicated privacy route answers 501; no request can be received, and the table has no organization column to scope a request to the institution that must answer it.

The enterprise integrations route is the generic factory over oauth_providers, a per-user table of provider account ids and access and refresh tokens with no organization column, under a name that advertises an organization integration list; the governance table denies it, so it serves nothing, and lifting that denial would expose tokens at the member floor.

The generic CRUD route declares orgScoped true over a table that has no organization column, so the factory adds no tenant predicate and every row of the table is visible to every organization once the read is allowed; the declared scope is a no-op.

The debug user-role route has no environment guard: it is the generic factory over organization_members, so it returns the roster rows of the organization (name, e-mail, phone, role, hire date, membership number, exemption reason) to a steward or above, and the caller own full row to a member, instead of a role check.

The Resend webhook looks the event up by provider message id and, when no message_log row carries it, logs a warning and still answers 200, so the provider does not retry and the delivery, bounce or complaint event is lost; an event that arrives before the sender has stored the provider message id is lost the same way.

The webhook sets message_log.status to the status of whichever event arrives last with no ordering rule, so a late sent, delivered or opened event overwrites a bounced, failed or complained status, and it updates in place a table whose schema comment declares it an immutable delivery log with no updatedAt.

The Svix message id is used only as a detail of the delivery-ledger row: the failed, unsubscribed and complained branches increment the campaign statistics on every redelivery of the same event, and the statistics are rewritten as a whole object from a value read earlier in the transaction, so a retry or a concurrent event changes the counters wrongly.

A complaint or suppression event updates the existing communication_preferences row of the one organization and recipient on the message log row, never inserts one and never writes a consent record or touches the distribution-list subscriptions, so a recipient with no preference row stays emailable while the audit record says the suppression was applied, and the same address is not suppressed in any other organization.

The delivery-ledger callback runs after the message_log transaction has committed and its result (recorded, duplicate, unmatched, ambiguous) is ignored, so a ledger failure answers 500 after the message_log, statistics and suppression have already changed and the provider retry repeats them, and an unmatched or ambiguous ledger event is acknowledged without a trace.

message_log.provider_message_id has neither an index nor a unique constraint, yet every webhook event selects by it with limit 1 under the system role, so each event scans the table and, if two rows ever carried the same id, the organization that receives the event is arbitrary.

The public contact route has no local store: it forwards the submission to HubSpot and answers ok true even when HUBSPOT_API_KEY is unset or the upsert fails (both return null and the handler skips the deal), so a visitor is told the message was received when no record of it exists anywhere but a log line that omits the message text.

The only control on the public contact route is a 20-per-hour limit keyed on cf-connecting-ip, x-real-ip or the first x-forwarded-for value, all request headers a caller can set unless an edge strips them, and the route has no captcha, honeypot or origin check, so a script can rotate the header and flood the CRM with contacts and deals.

Only the message field has a length bound on the public contact form: first name, last name, organization, role and inquiry type are unbounded strings forwarded to HubSpot (limited only by the 16 KiB body cap), and the visitor e-mail address and organization are written to the application log at info level.

The continuity archives and docs paths are byte-identical wrappers that re-export the document repository handlers behind a placeholder requireOrgAccess that always returns true and a mutation boundary that only checks that a method string exists: no archive, retention, continuity-plan or succession behaviour exists behind the names, a POST uploads an ordinary document, and the dead unauthorized branch reads as an access check that is not there.

The document repository list that the continuity paths serve has no row limit and no page, returns every non-deleted document row of the organization joined to its links, then runs a case-access lookup for each grievance-linked row and applies the linkedCase filter and the visibility policy in memory, so the cost grows with the size of the organization document store.

The continuity inheritance path advertises succession records but is the generic CRUD factory over pending_profiles, the pre-signup profile table holding the e-mail, Whop membership id and usage credits, which the CRUD governance table lists as DENIED, so every read and write answers 403 and no inheritance record can be read or written.

The inheritance route sets orgScoped true over pending_profiles, which has no organization column, so the factory adds no tenant predicate; the support_agent read floor and the DENIED governance entry are the only barriers, and lifting the governance entry would list the pre-signup e-mail and payment identifiers of every organization.

The deprecation registry served to every member names canonical replacements that have no route (/api/billing/reports, /api/strike/fund and /api/messages/[id]), repeats the sunset instant 2026-07-07 as a literal instead of the SUNSET_DATE constant, promises removal after that instant although routes it lists (payments webhook stripe, messaging preferences, financial vendors) still exist, and gives no sign that the list is hand-maintained.

The document-intake reaper, external-data-sync, location-retention and monthly-per-capita handlers export the same function as GET and POST, so a GET (the method a scheduler, browser prefetch or monitoring probe issues) expires intakes, deletes stored objects and location data, calls external providers or writes per-capita remittances while the route manifest records the GET as a read.

No scheduler entry in the repository invokes the document-intake reaper, external-data-sync, monthly-per-capita, observability-alerts or sla-watchdog handlers: apps/union-eyes/vercel.json schedules only calendar-sync and the ue-v2 apps.bicep cron job calls only deadline-reminders, so the jobs run only if an operator wires a trigger outside the source.

The two handlers listed in CRON_API_ROUTES (external-data-sync and monthly-per-capita) are first checked in proxy.ts against CRON_SECRET only with a plain !== comparison and the x-cron-secret header only, while the handler accepts CRON_SECRET_KEY first, a Bearer value too, and compares with timingSafeEqual; where only CRON_SECRET_KEY is set the edge refuses a correct caller, and the edge check is not constant time.

The only scheduler entry for calendar-sync (vercel.json, every 15 minutes) names the path with no method or secret, while the route exports POST only and verifyCronAuth reads only the x-cron-secret header, so a trigger that issues GET or presents the secret as a Bearer value is refused and no connection is synced.

The Google and Microsoft event import loops catch and discard the error of each event, and the cancelled-event handler discards its own error but the caller still adds one to the deleted count, so a failed event is missing from the local calendar while the connection is marked synced, the audit record reports the counts and the response shows no failure.

The Google import asks for at most 2500 events in one list call and never follows nextPageToken, and the cron never passes the stored sync token, so events beyond the first page are not imported while the connection is marked synced; the due list is selected without a lock or claim and nextSyncAt moves only at the end of each connection, so an overlapping run repeats the same provider calls.

The intake object finalizer selects only rows whose deletion_attempts are below INTAKE_MAX_DELETION_ATTEMPTS, so an abandoned object whose deletion keeps failing is never selected again after the limit, stays in storage, and the response reports only the failures of the current run.

The external-data-sync handler returns a plain object in every case, including the outer failure branch that sets success false, so the response is HTTP 200 whatever fails, and each sync method writes the external_data_sync_log row as completed even when records failed and never stores the collected error list, so the log does not show a partial or failed run.

syncContributionRates (and its sync-log rows) selects, updates and inserts through the plain tenant db handle while the wage, union-density and COLA methods run inside withSystemContext, so the contribution-rate part of the scheduled job runs without the system authority the other three parts were given and does not commit with a system transaction.

The 24-hour member location retention is enforced only by the location-retention handler, whose comments say it runs hourly, but no scheduler entry in the repository invokes it (vercel.json lists only calendar-sync and apps.bicep only deadline-reminders), so expired location points and geofence events are deleted only if an operator wires a trigger outside the source.

The deletion log written by the retention job records the run time as both the oldest and the newest deleted record date instead of the real dates, carries no organization, no list of affected members and no audit_log record, and the location tables have no organization column, so the evidence of what was deleted cannot show whose data or from when.

The retention job loads every expired user id from both tables without a limit and deletes user by user inside one system transaction, so a backlog (for example after the job did not run) is one long transaction holding locks on the live location tables.

The monthly per-capita job inserts and recalculates per_capita_remittances rows and marks them overdue for every organization with a parent, while the capability registry records the affiliate remittance capability (UE-FIN-AFFILIATE-REMITTANCES) as NOT_IMPLEMENTED and asks for a qualified model with institutional recipients, so remittance amounts and overdue states are produced without that model or any named financial officer decision.

The per-capita handler returns success true whatever the counts, the calculation catch block drops an organization whose calculation failed without a log or a count, the save step counts a failed write in errors with no record of which organization, and the handler runs markOverdueRemittances a second time after processMonthlyPerCapita already ran it, so the top-level overdueMarked value is the second sweep (normally zero) rather than the number marked.

The observability sweep writes each alert execution with status success, channels email and in_app and executionTimeMs 1, but the e-mail leg is only a notification_tracking row with status pending that no sender reads (notification-service names the table only in a comment and the process-notifications cron is a 501 stub), so the execution history shows an e-mail alert as delivered that was never sent.

The in-app alert is addressed to the pseudo-user system:observability-alerts and the tracking row names no recipient, and the alert rule is created with no recipient list, so no organization administrator is the target of an SLA-risk, ingestion-failure or payment-failure alert.

Each run counts the last 60 minutes and, because the rule frequency is every_occurrence and no earlier execution is consulted, emits a new execution, tracking row, in-app row and audit record for the same condition on every run, so a single failure window produces repeated alerts and unbounded rows.

The SLA watchdog emits sla_breached, sla_at_risk and sla_breach_risk on the in-process event bus under claim_events, an in-memory bus that drops an event with no subscriber, and no code subscribes to claim_events, so no steward, notification or record is produced for an overdue claim; the response counts breached and at-risk claims as though they had been handled.

The deadline is computed from claims.updated_at (falling back to created_at) as though it were the time of the last status change, and the claims table has no status-changed column, so any edit of a claim restarts its SLA clock and a claim that is touched often never breaches.

The watchdog selects every non-terminal claim of every organization with no limit, recomputes each deadline twice, and hands per-organization pilot metrics to promises it does not await, each recorded with no idempotency key as a metric insert and a separate audit insert, so a run answers before the writes finish and a run every minute adds new metric rows each time.

The interview list, the interview item (with its events and attached documents) and the document list return published and archived interviews to any member of the organization with no sensitivity level or consent condition: the whole row, including the full interview text, the retiring employee name, the retirement reason, the AI summary, the risk score and the user ids, and the transcripts and file URLs of the attachments, are returned for privileged, legal_sensitive and executive_confidential interviews, although SENSITIVITY_MIN_ROLE assigns those levels to officer and admin and the search, summary and AI routes enforce it.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any member of an organization that holds the union_knowledge_suite entitlement (the three reads are minRole member) can list up to 200 published or archived interviews and open any of them with its events and attached documents. Each response carries the whole row and the transcripts whatever sensitivity level an administrator assigned, so a legal_sensitive or executive_confidential interview is read in full by the lowest role.

potentialImpact.description: Bargaining advice, mediation tactics and case knowledge classified as privileged, legal sensitive or executive confidential, and the personal reason a named retiree left (including health), are readable by every member of the organization, defeating the classification an administrator sets and the legal-review expectation the governance module states.

existingContainment.summary: Only the status condition limits these reads: a member sees published and archived interviews and not the drafts of other users. No sensitivity level, consent or role-per-level condition exists on the list, item or document path.

releaseDisposition.justification: The classification that governance records exists to restrict who reads an interview, and three member-floor reads disclose the content of every classified interview in full to the whole organization. The status condition hides only unpublished drafts, so it does not contain the exposure, and the sibling routes that do enforce the level show the intended behaviour is absent here.

defectRegister.title: Publication inserts an active knowledge_base row holding the full interview text and the retiring employee name for every sensitivity level and consent state (isPublishAllowed is defined and tested but never called), and the re-index route rewrites that row from the interview; the knowledge-base list and item routes return active rows to any authenticated user of the organization and of its child organizations with no sensitivity, consent, entitlement or role condition, so the classification and consent attached to the interview do not follow the copy.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An administrator publishing a reviewed interview creates a knowledge_base row with the whole text; GET /api/knowledge-base/[id] then returns its content to any authenticated user whose organization, or whose parent organization, owns the row, and GET /api/knowledge-base lists it and matches the content with q. No entitlement, role or sensitivity condition is applied on those routes, so the copy of a legal_sensitive interview is read by every member and by members of child organizations.

potentialImpact.description: The full text of an interview, with the name of the retiring member, becomes readable outside the knowledge-transfer entitlement by every member of the organization and by the members of every child organization of a federation, regardless of the sensitivity level and consent the interview record carries.

existingContainment.summary: The knowledge-base row is created with isPublic false, and the AI search and AI summarize routes withhold exit-interview rows below the interview sensitivity role; the knowledge-base list and item routes apply neither, so the containment does not reach the read that discloses the copy.

releaseDisposition.justification: The copy is created by the publication step for every interview, is active at once, and is served in full by routes that any authenticated user can call and that cross to the parent organization. The sibling AI routes already withhold these rows below the interview role, so the gap is on the knowledge-base reads, and because it discloses to members of other organizations as well as to the whole tenant it is release blocking.

defectRegister.title: The governance route changes consent and sensitivity on the exit_interviews row only: withdrawing consent leaves the knowledge_base row active with its content and embedding, the re-index refusal marks indexing skipped without touching that row, and neither the keyword search nor the semantic search carries a consent condition, so an interview whose retiree consent is withdrawn is still returned by search and still served by the knowledge-base routes.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An administrator can set consentGranted to false on a published interview, and the route reports success and an indexingEligible flag, but the knowledge_base copy and its embedding stay active and every member who can pass the sensitivity floor of search still receives the interview, because the search queries filter on status and sensitivity and never on consent.

potentialImpact.description: A retiring member who withdraws consent to the use of their interview in search and retrieval has no effect on what the organization serves: the stored copy, the vector and the keyword match remain available to members, and the audit record shows a consent change that changed nothing.

existingContainment.summary: A reclassification to a higher sensitivity level is honoured by the search queries, which test the current level of the interview on every request; consent has no equivalent condition.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: An organization records the withdrawal of a retiree consent on an interview that is already published or indexed; from then the withdrawal has no effect on search results, the knowledge-base copy or the stored embedding.
releaseDisposition.justification: The route advertises consent control and the effect of a withdrawal is nil, but the exposure needs a withdrawal to be recorded on a published interview, which no organization is known to have done; once one does, the retiree is still served to members, so the defect blocks release on that condition and not before.

defectRegister.title: After the publication transaction commits, a setImmediate job sends the interview text to the AI control plane for expertise extraction for every sensitivity level and consent state (only the embedding step is gated by isIndexingAllowed), with data class internal, no intent or outcome audit record, and every error swallowed, then updates expertiseTags, continuityRiskScore and continuityRiskFlags on the row with no status condition and no audit record.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Each publication by an administrator (minRole admin, entitlement required) triggers one model call carrying the title, lessons, bargaining and mediation advice and topics of the interview, even for privileged, legal_sensitive or executive_confidential interviews and an interview without retiree consent, and then writes model-derived columns on the interview; the summarize and re-index routes record an intent audit before any provider call, and this one records nothing.

potentialImpact.description: Content that governance marks as requiring legal review or executive access, and content of a retiree who has not consented, is disclosed to a model provider through the AI control plane without a record that the disclosure happened or who triggered it.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: An organization publishes an interview classified privileged, legal_sensitive or executive_confidential, or one whose retiree has not consented, while the ue-expertise-extraction profile resolves to a model provider outside the control of the organization; each such publication then discloses the text to that provider with no audit record.
releaseDisposition.justification: The extraction runs on every publication and ignores both gates that the same job applies to indexing, and it leaves no record, which is the property that makes a disclosure reviewable. Whether the text leaves the organization control depends on how the control plane profile is wired, which the source does not fix, so the defect blocks release when a classified or non-consented interview is published against an external provider.

defectRegister.title: When the model reply for expertise extraction is not valid JSON, extractExpertise returns a fallback profile with continuitySensitivity medium and an empty undocumented-workflow list, and the publish job turns it into continuityRiskScore 40 and writes it to the interview as if it had been assessed; the failure leaves no event and no flag, so analytics and the risk views count an unassessed interview as a medium-risk one.

The governance route records consentGranted from an administrator body flag with consentGrantedBy set to the administrator user id and an optional note kept only in the event, so the retiring member is never identified as the grantor and no consent evidence is required, and any single administrator can lower a published interview from legal_sensitive or executive_confidential to public_internal, or grant its consent, with no second approver and no legal-review step; the interview row also keeps the previous values from a read made before the transaction.

The create schema has no sensitivity or consent field, so every interview is born public_internal with consent false, and neither submit, review nor publish requires that a classification decision was recorded: an interview that no administrator ever classified is published at the lowest level and, through the unconditioned reads, is visible to every member.

The review route refuses only the creator of the interview, but any officer who edited the draft (steward and above may edit any draft) or submitted it, and who did not create it, may review it, the table records no submitter, and the publish route compares neither the reviewer nor the creator with the publisher, so one administrator can edit, review and publish the same interview although the route comment calls the review an independent check.

The document attach route accepts any URL whose host is the platform shared storage account or its subdomains, localhost or 127.0.0.1, stores it with the client-supplied mime type and size, and never checks that the blob exists, belongs to the organization or has the declared type, so a steward can register another organization blob path or a loopback URL as an interview document that every member who can read the interview then receives.

The document attach route refuses only published and archived interviews, so a steward can attach a document and a transcript of up to 100000 characters to an interview that has already been reviewed and is awaiting publication, material that the reviewer never saw and that is published with the interview without a second review.

The keyword search applies the row limit (twice the requested limit) in SQL and filters out the interviews the caller role may not read afterwards in memory, so a member whose first matching rows are of a higher level receives fewer results, or none, although readable interviews match, and total reports the filtered length as if it were the match count.

The re-index route returns status 200 with indexed false and the raw error string (String(err)) when the embedding or the database write fails, and the same shape for a governance refusal, so a failure is indistinguishable by status from a refusal and internal error text reaches the response.

The summary generator parses the model reply with JSON.parse and no shape check, and on a parse failure returns a fixed placeholder sentence with empty lists; the route stores operationalSummary as ai_summary, records the event "AI knowledge summary generated" and returns 200, so a failed generation is stored, searched by the keyword search and shown to members as the AI summary of the interview, and a reply without operationalSummary writes nothing while still recording the event.

The summarize route sends the interview lessons, best practices, bargaining, mediation and incoming-officer advice to the AI control plane with data class internal for any consent state and for legal_sensitive and executive_confidential interviews when the caller is an administrator, and never reads consentGranted or containsPii, so the consent that gates the embedding does not gate this model call.

The summarize and copilot routes call the model with only the union_knowledge_suite entitlement and the default organization rate limit: they apply no guardAiFeature feature flag, no AI safety check of the caller text and no per-user AI rate limit, which the other advisory AI routes of the application declare, and the copilot passes the free text query and up to twenty caller-supplied prior messages straight into the model input.

ue_copilot_conversations has no user column, so any steward lists the conversations of the whole organization, reads the full message history of any conversation id, and a POST with another conversation id appends the caller messages and the model answer to it; the questions that officers and administrators put to the copilot are readable and writable by every steward.

The copilot returns an evidence envelope built from the aggregate counts and fixed sentences (three reasoning steps whose first claims a retrieval from published exit interviews that the model never received, fixed assumptions, evidence confidence high) around a model answer whose claims are linked to none of it, and the envelope is not persisted (explainabilityRef null), so the history shows no lineage although the engine header says each response is persisted with its explainability envelope.

The copilot builds the model input from priorMessages sent by the client, with roles user or assistant, and not from the stored conversation, so a caller can supply assistant turns that were never generated and the answer is conditioned on a history that differs from the persisted conversation.

The topic graph and the dependency propagation map behind the graph query, simulation, scenario and mitigation comparison routes are built from every published interview with no sensitivity or consent condition, so the topic labels, the contributing roles and the single-source findings drawn from privileged, legal_sensitive and executive_confidential interviews are returned to stewards (graph query) and officers.

Every preset scenario carries an empty affectedNodeIds, so the simulator takes its no-match branch for all four scenario types and returns the fixed minimal result (immediate impact 20, severity low, autonomous recovery probability 85, empty domain impacts and timeline) for each; the scenarios route reports best case, worst case, average impact 20 and four hard-coded cross-scenario mitigations for a retirement wave, rapid turnover, governance transition or vendor disruption as a modelled comparison, and the preset affectedRoles and timelineWeeks are never read.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An officer of an organization with the union_knowledge_suite entitlement who posts any of the four scenario types receives HTTP 200 with a comparison whose every figure comes from the fixed minimal result: low severity, an average impact of 20 and an 85 percent chance of autonomous recovery, whatever the organization published interviews say; the only hint is the executive summary text asking the reader to review parameters.

potentialImpact.description: Leadership asking what a retirement wave or a vendor disruption would do to continuity is told, as a modelled outcome, that the impact is low and recovery is likely, which can postpone documentation, cross-training and succession work that the organization actual single-source knowledge calls for.

existingContainment.summary: The no-match result carries an executive summary that says the scenario parameters did not match the available organizational knowledge, and one immediate action asking the reader to review the parameters and retry, so a careful reader of the text can see it is not a model result; no status or flag in the response says so.

evidence.quote: executiveSummary: 'Scenario parameters did not match available organizational knowledge. Review and retry.',

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: An organization uses the scenario comparison, in the interface or in a report, to decide or to show how a retirement wave, turnover or vendor disruption would affect continuity; the output is the same fixed result for every organization, so it blocks release as soon as the route is offered as a modelling feature.
releaseDisposition.justification: The route cannot produce a real simulation for any of its four inputs, so every response is a reassuring constant presented under the shape of a comparison. Only the text of the summary tells a careful reader, which limits the harm to readers who act on the figures; the route is reachable by officers of entitled organizations only, so it blocks release on the condition that the scenario feature is offered as a model of the organization.

defectRegister.title: The simulation route passes affectedNodeIds, an unvalidated array of free strings, to a simulator that returns the fixed minimal result (impact 20, severity low, recovery 85) with status 200 when none matches a node, and never reads affectedRoles, context or timelineWeeks, so a mistyped or stale node id and every role-based scenario read as a low-impact simulation.

The mitigation comparison computes exposure reduction, resilience gain and the recommended scenario from a fixed effectiveness table by mitigation and node type and a fixed investment bonus (0.7, 1.0, 1.2), labels the per-domain confidence from that constant (high at 0.7 and above), returns an empty result with no error when the targetNodeIds match no node, and ranks and recommends a scenario from them, so the projections and the recommendation reflect the table and not evidence of the organization.

The graph query route validates and forwards category, roleFilter, depthLimit and explanationLevel, and the reasoner reads none of them (only minimumRiskLevel, in the isolated knowledge query), so a caller who narrows by category or role, limits the depth or asks for a brief or exhaustive explanation receives the same unfiltered findings for every value.

The cognition memory POST stores a memory type such as simulation_snapshot or resilience_baseline, a resilience score and an unbounded payload exactly as the officer supplied them, with no author column on ue_cognition_memory and no check against the real simulation or index, and the load builds the resilience timeline and change-from-previous figures from those asserted scores, so organizational memory and the timeline can hold figures nobody computed.

ue_reasoning_sessions records no creator, so the sessions list returns every session of the organization, with its context description, graph state, annotations and linked memory ids, to any steward, and no route limits a session to the person who opened it.

The analytics timeline reports a consent coverage rate of 100 for any month with no interviews and a current exposure score of 0 when no interview has a score, so empty months and an unassessed organization read as the best case, and it loads every interview and event of the last twelve months into memory with no limit.

The expertise map (steward floor), the cascade analysis, the decision brief, the continuity risk report and the governance timeline (officer floor) read the published, or for the timeline every, exit interview of the organization without selecting or testing its sensitivityLevel and return the topic, expertise tag and role labels, the single-source flags with the role and risk score of the one interview behind a tag, the ids of the interviews awaiting review, and the free-text notes of review events, although the consent policy requires the admin role for legal_sensitive and executive_confidential interviews and the steward or officer role for restricted and privileged ones; nothing in these routes applies that table.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An officer (a steward for the expertise map) of an organization that holds the union_knowledge_suite entitlement receives, in one call and with no sensitivity filter, topic and expertise labels, roles, per-tag risk scores and review notes derived from every interview of the organization, including legal_sensitive and executive_confidential ones that the consent policy reserves for the admin role.

potentialImpact.description: A steward or officer below the role that the sensitivity policy names learns the subjects, roles and review commentary of a departing member whose interview was classified legal_sensitive or executive_confidential; a single-source row identifies the one interviewee role and risk score.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: The union_knowledge_suite entitlement is granted to an organization whose exit-interview archive holds a published interview classified above public_internal, at which point a steward or officer reads derived content the sensitivity policy withholds from that role.
releaseDisposition.justification: The routes are role- and entitlement-gated, so the exposure stays inside one organization and needs an entitled organization with sensitive interviews; no filter, redaction or consent test limits what the derived responses carry, so the disclosure happens as soon as that condition is true and must be closed before the entitlement is sold.

defectRegister.title: The cross-domain-correlation route answers 200 for every organization with the same five correlation pairs, strengths 0.75, 0.65, 0.60, 0.70 and 0.80, the same three fragility indicators, the same three operating insights and the narrative that the organization shows strong correlations between governance discipline, continuity capability and resilience maturity; the only value read from the organization is the count of cognition memory entries, so no correlation is computed and an empty organization is told the same thing.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any officer of an organization holding the union_knowledge_suite entitlement receives HTTP 200 with five fixed correlation strengths, indicators and a narrative that reports strong correlations as a finding about that organization, whatever its data; only entriesAnalyzed comes from the database.

potentialImpact.description: Governance and continuity decisions can cite correlation strengths and a narrative that no analysis produced, and an organization with no data at all is told that its governance and continuity are strongly correlated.

releaseDisposition.justification: The route returns a fabricated analytical result with a success status instead of refusing the capability, and the role floor and entitlement only limit who is told it; no part of the source marks the output as sample or placeholder, so the harm is present for every entitled officer and does not depend on a later condition.

defectRegister.title: The continuity forecast projects twelve months from three fixed monthly rates (concentration +0.3, governance -0.5 and redundancy erosion -0.2) and subtracts the negative erosion from the average redundancy, so projected redundancy rises every month and projected health rises about 0.6 points a month whatever the data, which makes trendDirection read improving for every organization whose projected health stays below 100; its historical series is rebuilt from published interview dates with a fixed vendor concentration of 40 and a fixed fallback point (health 60, five single-source nodes), and the decision brief executive summary states that trend direction as a forecast of continuity health.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An officer of an organization holding the union_knowledge_suite entitlement receives, from the forecasting route and inside the decision brief executive summary that the continuity planning workspace renders, twelve monthly health projections and a trend direction that improve by construction, together with a historical series that is partly fixed literals.

potentialImpact.description: A union can read a continuity forecast that says its position will improve when no input supports the claim, and defer succession and documentation work on the strength of a projection whose direction was fixed by a sign error and constant rates.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: The union_knowledge_suite entitlement is granted to an organization, or any workspace, report or export presents the forecast or the decision brief summary that repeats it, so that a reader acts on a projection that improves by construction.
releaseDisposition.justification: The numbers are computed from real counts but the projection step uses constants and a sign inversion, so its direction does not depend on the organization; the harm needs an entitled organization that acts on the forecast, which is the condition under which this blocks release.

defectRegister.title: When an organization has no published interview, or none that yields a topic, the dependency map has no nodes and the resilience index divides by zero: overallScore and the dimension scores are NaN (null in JSON), statusFromScore(NaN) returns strong, maturity reads initial, the decision brief states strong continuity resilience with a score of NaN out of 100, the federated benchmark places the organization in the nascent cohort at the 97th percentile, and the forecast projections are NaN with a stable trend.

The continuity risk route sends the role, years of service, title, expertise tags and topics of every published exit interview, whatever its sensitivityLevel or consent flag, to a model through getAiClient under the system organization id with dataClass internal, without guardAiFeature, an AI safety check or an AI interaction audit record; it parses the model reply with JSON.parse and no schema check and returns the flags as they come, answers 200 with empty flags and a manual-review sentence when the reply is not JSON, and lets a failed generate call surface as a 500.

The behaviour pattern, governance culture, learning archetype, governance adaptation, governance coherence, governance momentum and adaptive resilience routes derive their scores, postures, archetypes and narratives from counts, types and dates of cognition memory entries and reasoning sessions, whose memoryType, title and resilienceScoreAtCapture an officer chooses when saving them through the memory route; an organization with no entries is reported as governance stagnant (archetype score 100, strongly characterized), so the output measures use of the analytics tools and officer-entered scores, not governance decisions, and is presented as the governance culture, momentum, coherence and archetype of the organization.

Every cognitionRoute operation returns an explainability envelope whose confidence band comes from a constant score of 60 (moderate) written in defineFoundationalEngine and defaulted in adaptLegacyEngine, whose evidence, reasoning, assumptions and governance implications are always empty arrays because the engine definitions pass none to buildExplainabilityEnvelope, and which carries no per-organization data-sufficiency signal, so the envelope advertises explainability and a confidence that the engine does not compute.

The federated benchmark reports an estimatedPercentile, a cohort and cohort-average dimension comparisons by interpolating the resilience score on an eight-point reference distribution and six cohort averages written as literals with the description based on organizational governance research and no named source, population or date, so the response states that the organization sits at the Nth percentile although no population exists behind the figure, and only the disclaimer text says no cross-organization data is used.

The expertise map rates a domain critical when one interview mentions its tag, reports averageRiskScore 0 when no interview carries a score, and returns the roles of the one interview behind a single-source tag; the continuity risk report returns overallRiskScore 0 for an organization with no interview, scores coverage gaps against the literal role list steward, chief_steward, officer and admin, and caps each term of the score with fixed weights; the decision brief marks its evidence confidence high as a literal, so the ratings are fixed rules over tag counts presented as measured risk.

The cascade analysis builds regulatoryRisks by prefixing Regulatory continuity risk: to the identifier of every node impacted by a governance or compliance node, whatever that node is, returns the same three recommendation strings for every organization, and classifies governance and compliance nodes by substring keywords over interview tags (a tag containing meeting or report is a governance node), so the regulatory risk list is a label template and not a regulatory assessment.

The governance coherence profile sets overlapScore 50, ambiguousAuthority 40, duplicationLevel 30, the evidence Baseline overlap analysis, a stable trend on every dimension, an empty conflictingPolicies list and fixed breakdown frequency 60 and recovery time 14 whatever the data, and the governance momentum profile computes its five indicators as entry counts divided by fixed denominators (10, 10, 8, 30 and 50) with no time dimension, labelling a small count decelerating or volatile, so neither measures coherence or momentum over time.

buildResilienceRoadmap, which the adaptive resilience engine calls, tests the documentation strategy with the expression score ?? 0 < 65, which parses as score ?? (0 < 65), so the strategy is added whenever the documentation score is any nonzero number (including 100) and withheld when the score is 0 or NaN, the opposite of the intent that a low documentation score selects it.

The governance timeline reads at most 500 events and every interview created in the six-month window with no limit, then computes eventTypeCounts, governanceUpdatesLast30Days and the stale review counts from the capped event list and the interview list as they stand, so counts silently understate for an organization with more than 500 events in the window while the interview read grows without bound, and the totals carry no truncation marker.

The succession GET reads every published exit interview of the organization whatever its sensitivity level or consent flag, builds a prompt from each role, years of service, title, topics and risk flags, sends it to the model provider on every call, and returns the model text (gaps, priorities, recommendations, executive summary) to any officer, while the sibling summarize route refuses an interview unless the caller holds the role its sensitivity level requires (admin for legal_sensitive and executive_confidential).

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An officer of an organization that holds the union_knowledge_suite entitlement calls GET succession (the continuity cockpit does so on load): every published interview, including those classified privileged, legal_sensitive and executive_confidential, is sent to the model provider and summarized back to the officer, below the admin floor that the summarize route applies to the same interviews.

potentialImpact.description: Titles, topics, risk flags, roles and years of service of departing members and officers, including legal-sensitive and executive-confidential interviews, leave the organization for a model provider and come back as prose that an officer who could not read those interviews can read.

existingContainment.summary: Only published interviews are read, the caller must be an officer in an organization that holds the union_knowledge_suite entitlement, and the prompt carries no retiring employee name or key lessons; nothing restricts the interviews by sensitivity level or consent.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: An organization holding the union_knowledge_suite entitlement has published an exit interview classified privileged, legal_sensitive or executive_confidential, and a steward (topic graph, propagation) or an officer (succession, aggregators) calls the route: the text of that interview is then reflected to a reader below the role the interview requires.
releaseDisposition.justification: The route is live behind an officer floor and an entitlement, so the harm needs an organization with the entitlement and an interview published at a restricted level; where that is true the disclosure is complete (every such interview, every call), reaches an external processor and an under-privileged reader, and nothing in the route stops it, so release is blocked for such an organization until the sensitivity floor is applied before the model call.

defectRegister.title: The succession GET wraps the provider call in no audit record (no performAuditedOperation, persistAtomicAudit or auditLog, unlike the summarize route), caches nothing and sets no route rate limit, so each page load of the cockpit sends the full published-interview prompt to the model again, only the default organization limit of 1200 requests per 5 minutes applies, and no record shows who triggered which disclosure.

The model reply is parsed with JSON.parse and cast to the report shape with no schema check, so its five fields are returned verbatim whatever their type or content (the prompt alone forbids naming individuals), nothing in the response marks them as model-generated, and a parse failure is swallowed into an HTTP 200 with empty gap lists and a canned executive summary instead of an error.

The succession report scores readiness from how many published exit interviews exist for each of five fixed roles, not from any successor, handover or documentation record: an organization with no interviews scores 50 of 100, a role is "adequate" with two interviews and no stored risk score (average risk 0), "minimal" with one high-risk interview, roles outside the five are skipped, and more departures therefore raise the readiness shown.

The topic graph and the propagation map select every published exit interview of the organization with no sensitivity-level or consent condition and return each interview topic and expertise tag as a node label with the contributing roles, so a steward (and an officer through the aggregator) reads the topic text and role of interviews classified legal_sensitive or executive_confidential that the interview routes release only to an admin; only the AI search route applies the readable-levels filter.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: A steward of an organization holding the union_knowledge_suite entitlement calls GET topic-graph or propagation (the topic-graph and simulation screens do): every topic and expertise tag of every published interview, with the roles that contributed it and a single-source flag, comes back whatever the interview sensitivity level, and an officer receives the same payloads through organizational-cognition.

potentialImpact.description: Topic and expertise tags of legal-sensitive and executive-confidential interviews, with the role of the departing person and a flag that the knowledge sits with one source, are readable by stewards and officers who may not read the interview, which can reveal what a restricted interview is about and who it concerns.

existingContainment.summary: Only published interviews are read and the caller must hold the steward role and the union_knowledge_suite entitlement; the output is tags and counts, not interview text, and nothing restricts it by sensitivity level.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: An organization holding the union_knowledge_suite entitlement has published an exit interview classified privileged, legal_sensitive or executive_confidential, and a steward (topic graph, propagation) or an officer (succession, aggregators) calls the route: the text of that interview is then reflected to a reader below the role the interview requires.
releaseDisposition.justification: The harm needs the entitlement and an interview published at a restricted level; where both hold, any steward reads the topics and roles of interviews that the interview routes reserve for officers or admins on every call, and the route has no sensitivity check to limit it, so release is blocked for such an organization until derived output follows the interview sensitivity floor.

defectRegister.title: The topic graph, propagation map and succession report return roles, years of service, risk scores and single-source flags with no minimum cohort size and no labor-safety assertion (the routes bypass the engine wrapper): a topic or role that comes from one published interview names the contributing role of that one departing person, and the succession role row for a role with one interview carries that person years of service and risk score.

The propagation map treats two tags that appear together in two interviews as a dependency whose direction is whichever tag has the lower interview count, marks a tag in one interview as a sole expert whose loss "would create compliance gap", and derives path impact, exposure and recovery weeks from fixed formulas, so inferred statements about dependency, sole ownership and recovery time are returned as findings with no record of an actual process, system or owner.

Topic categories are assigned by substring match of free-text tags against keyword lists in a fixed order (for example the three-letter compliance keyword esa matches inside any tag containing those letters), and a tag seen in one interview whose category comes out governance or compliance is marked critical sensitivity, so unrelated tags can raise critical bottleneck findings.

An unknown nodeId makes the propagation handler throw a plain Error that withApi answers as an unexpected 500 instead of a 404, nodeId and analysisType are read from the query with no schema, an unrecognised analysisType (and coupling) silently returns the full map, and a nodeId answers a node view whatever analysisType says.

The topic graph, propagation map, resilience index and succession analyzer select every published exit interview of the organization with no limit, the topic graph builds a pair edge for every two tags of each interview, and the succession prompt concatenates every interview, so the cost and the model prompt grow without bound with the interview count.

For an organization with no published interview the resilience index divides by the zero node count: the knowledge-redundancy, documentation and governance scores are NaN (null in the JSON), statusFromScore(NaN) answers strong for those dimensions and for the overall status, and the resilience roadmap built on it prints "strong continuity maturity (NaN/100)", projects NaN, and recommends no documentation strategy.

The index trend is stable or degrading from one snapshot (single-source nodes over 40 percent of nodes) and can never be improving, the "Estimated doc quality" component is 25, 50 or 75 from the interview count alone, and the maturity level and status are label cut-offs on a score built from node counts, yet the response presents them as a trend, a quality estimate and a maturity assessment.

The roadmap tests the documentation dimension with `score ?? 0 < 65`, which returns the score itself, so the documentation strategy is recommended for every non-zero score (including 100) and not for a score of 0, and the projected resilience, governance and dependency gains of each strategy are literal numbers from a per-strategy table (for example 18, 10 and 15) summed into a projected score, not a model of this organization.

Every engine adapter passes a fixed confidence score of 60 (the foundational adapter hard-codes it, the dynamics adapter defaults to it and no engine supplies a payload-based score) and supplies no evidence, reasoning, assumptions or governance implications, so the explainability block of each response reports moderate confidence with empty evidence and reasoning whatever the data, including an organization with no memory entries, and the labor-safety assertion is called with a literal organizational scope that cannot fail.

The memory-based engines compute only from ue_cognition_memory rows that an officer creates through POST cognition-memory with a self-declared memory type and an optional self-declared resilience score between 0 and 100 (saveCognitionMemory has that one caller), so trajectory, learning, personality, habit, mitigation, dynamics and coordination results restate typed entries and typed numbers as measured organizational condition, and a score absent from an entry removes it from the timeline.

The systems-dynamics, operational-coordination, operating-rhythms, multi-domain-cognition and operational-trust engines write literal values into their profiles that depend on no stored record (consistency 50 and 60, stabilization signal confidence 75 and 70, coordination frequency 70 and 50, response times of 5, 7 and 3 days, adherence 75, variance 30, stabilization 14 days, integration scores 50 to 70, reasoning-chain confidence 70 and 65, fixed trust indicators such as Reliable mitigation execution), so a reader cannot tell a measured field from a constant.

Coordination efficiency, rhythm stability and predictability, systems velocity and governance stabilization are the number of memory entries divided by 30, trust is that number divided by 20, rhythm frequency is weekly at 12 governance entries whatever their dates, adaptationsPerYear is a plain count, mitigation cycle days is 90 divided by the mitigation count, and elasticity indicators are the share of each typed category, so adding rows raises the figure and none of them observes coordination, cadence, recovery or trust.

The operational-trust engine derives all four trust figures from the entry count, subtracting 5 for follow-through (negative with no entries) and adding 5 for mitigation execution (105 from 20 entries), always lists "Consistent governance behavior", "Reliable mitigation execution" and "Stable accountability" as indicators, and states "moderate operational trust" for an organization with no entries at all.

The institutional-precedent and procedural-continuity engines return the same literal profile for every organization (recurring precedents Governance protocols, Continuity procedures and Mitigation patterns; precedent chains with impact 75 and 60; fragility score 45, redundancy 50, procedure resilience 55, continuity risk moderate), reading ue_cognition_memory only to print an entry count and to set undocumented_processes to the count divided by 10, yet both are wrapped in an explainability envelope as analysis of the organization own records and shown on the operating-intelligence screen.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: An officer of any organization holding the union_knowledge_suite entitlement receives the same fixed precedent and procedural-fragility profile whatever that organization has recorded, directly from the two routes and through organizational-cognition, which the operating-intelligence workspace reads and displays as procedural and precedent panels.

potentialImpact.description: A union officer is shown a fragility score, a continuity-risk level, recurring precedents and precedent chains as findings about the union own procedures and decisions when they are constants, which can steer continuity planning and governance reviews with no basis in the union records.

releaseDisposition.justification: The constants are returned on every call with no data dependence, wrapped as an explainability envelope with moderate confidence, and displayed in a screen that fetches them; the only limits are the officer floor and the entitlement, which restrict who is misled but not whether the content is real, so a union that buys the module is told invented findings and release is blocked until the engines compute from records or are removed from the surface.

defectRegister.title: The governance personality engine returns the type Resilience-Fragile (with the identity statement "This organization operates as a Resilience-Fragile institution" and a strategic focus) whenever fewer than two entries and sessions exist, so an organization that has simply not recorded anything is characterized with a named personality instead of insufficient data, and every other dimension score is a weighted count of the typed entries.

Mitigation effectiveness rates an intervention by the difference between its typed score and the score of the next later entry of any type that carries one, with no limit on the interval (daysToObservableEffect can be months), no control for other entries, and a resilienceRoi, so a score change is presented as the effect of the mitigation and rated highly_effective, ineffective or counterproductive.

The learning trajectory forecast extrapolates linearly from the first and last typed scores with a momentum multiplier, from as few as two points, and attaches a confidence range of plus or minus min(3 per month, 20) that is a literal formula rather than an interval from the data, then estimates months to the next maturity milestone from it, so a forecast with no statistical basis is presented with a confidence range.

The orchestrator isolates a failing engine into a failures list carrying the raw exception message, and both aggregator routes return that list inside an HTTP 200 body, so a database or provider error text reaches the client and a response with missing engines is a success.

Each call to the two aggregator routes runs all 28 engines (17 foundational and 11 dynamics) in parallel, and most of them each reload cognition memory or the published-interview graph for the same organization, with no cache of the envelopes and no route rate limit beyond the default organization limit, so one request multiplies into dozens of tenant transactions.

The narrative route states that each narrative is derived from institutional evidence at a confidence band, but the envelopes carry no evidence, reasoning or governance implication, so every summary reads "Derived from 0 institutional evidence items with moderate confidence", the headline is the first sentence of fixed interpretation guidance, key reasoning and review signals are empty, and the executive briefing ranking sees identical scores for every engine.

The /api/exports, /api/exports/[id], /api/exports/csv, /api/exports/excel and /api/exports/pdf routes are the same generic crudRoutes configuration over the reports table: the csv, excel and pdf path segments are cosmetic, no handler reads any source table, builds a CSV, workbook or PDF, streams a file or sets a content type, and the reports table has no format, file or job column although a report_format enum of pdf, excel, csv, json and html exists, so a POST to /api/exports/pdf answers success with a report definition row and a GET answers a list of definitions, and nothing is exported.

The export suite reads of the reports table are open to any member of an entitled organization: the table has no owner or personal column and the routes declare no ownerColumn, so the low-role guard stays open and a member receives every report definition of the organization, including definitions the author kept private (isPublic false), written by other users, in the financial, members and claims categories, with the whole config JSON that names the data sources, fields and filters of each report.

The export suite create and update take the whole request body into the reports row: a steward can create a report of reportType system, mark it a template or public, and set runCount, lastRunAt and templateId, and the update has no owner condition and blocks no field, so any steward can rewrite any report of the organization, including its createdBy, updatedBy, config, runCount and lastRunAt, which makes the author and usage columns of a report definition unreliable.

The reports table has no status column, so the administrator delete of an export suite report removes the row (hard delete) and the in-transaction audit record it writes lists an empty field set, which leaves no stored copy of the name, category or config of the deleted report definition.

The evidence export, described as an evidence pack summary suitable for procurement and security review, returns policy_checks (grievance creation, status transition, escalation, arbitration seal and evidence immutability as enforced, cross_org_access as denied), org_isolation (enforced true, enforced at the db, route and audit layers, cross_org_read_attempts_blocked true) and an sbom marked available as string and boolean literals of the handler: the handler reads no database, test result, policy engine, sealed bundle or build artifact, so each assertion is returned whether or not the control holds, and the build timestamp, commit and version are environment fallbacks (process start time, local, 0.0.0).

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any authenticated caller whose organization role is not member and not empty, including the deprecated guest role, receives a 200 JSON document that states cross-organization access is denied and organization isolation is enforced at three layers, with no check behind any of the statements.

potentialImpact.description: A procurement or security reviewer, or a control-plane evidence adapter that consumes the same shape, receives hard-coded assurances of tenant isolation and evidence immutability as if they were measured, and can rely on them for a purchase, audit or compliance decision.

existingContainment.summary: The handler refuses unauthenticated callers and callers whose organization role is member or empty, and its header states that the sealed evidence bundle is produced by the evidence pipeline, which limits who receives the snapshot but does not make any of its statements true.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: The snapshot is given to a procurement or security reviewer, or consumed by a platform evidence-pack adapter, as evidence of tenant isolation and evidence immutability before those controls are measured by the evidence pipeline and the statements are derived from that result.
releaseDisposition.justification: The route is live for non-member staff and its output is built for external review, so the harm is a false assurance rather than a data leak; no cross-tenant data is disclosed and the audience is role restricted, so the release is blocked only when the snapshot is used as evidence of controls that no code in the handler verifies.

defectRegister.title: The evidence export labels the pack with the orgId query parameter (default unscoped) and never reads the organization of the session, so a caller can have the pack that asserts cross-organization access is denied issued under the identifier of any other organization, or of no organization, and the isolation assertions are not tied to the caller organization.

The evidence export role gate is a deny list of the two spellings member and MEMBER: every other organization role string passes, including the deprecated guest role and any role string that is not in the canonical list, and the response gives the deployed version and commit.

The evidence export records each issue only by incrementing a process-local counter (recordEvidenceExport), with no audit row, actor or organization, so who obtained the pack and when is lost on restart and is not reproducible across instances.

The /api/external-data and /api/external-data/lrb routes are the same generic crudRoutes configuration over external_accounts, the chart of accounts that accounting providers synchronize, which the CRUD governance table lists as DENIED, so every GET and POST answers 403 before any query; the lrb path name suggests labour relations board data but no board source is read by either route, and the table-level register of the repository still describes both routes as the live select and insert path of the table.

The external document download returns a read-only storage link in the JSON body with the default sixty-minute lifetime (generateSasUrl is called without an expiry), not bound to the caller, address or grant: the grant, the expiry and the revocation are checked only when the link is issued, so the link keeps working for the rest of its hour after the document grant is revoked or expires and can be passed to a person who holds no grant, and the audit row records the issue of the link, not a read of the blob.

The external document download releases the document version with the highest version number at the time of the request: the external_document_access_grants table has no version column and the handler binds the grant to the document only, so a revision uploaded after the grant was made, which no one reviewed for disclosure to the outside party, is released under the earlier grant.

The extensions item read selects the whole api_integrations row and returns it as it is to any member of the organization: the credentials jsonb column (documented as encrypted, though no code in the application writes or encrypts it), the SFTP host, port and path and the API endpoint of an HR, payroll or accounting connection are returned with no projection and no redaction, unlike the sibling SSO list, which masks its secrets.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any active member of an organization (minRole member, no entitlement, no further check) who holds an integration uuid of their own organization receives the whole api_integrations row, including the credentials column, the SFTP location and the API endpoint; the organization predicate keeps the response inside the tenant, and the application has no route that creates the rows, so the response carries credentials only for a row that exists.

potentialImpact.description: A member who is not an officer could read the stored credentials of the organization HR, payroll or accounting connections and use them against the external system, reaching employee and pay data that no member role grants.

existingContainment.summary: The application exposes no route that creates or imports api_integrations rows, so a row, and therefore credentials, exists only if it was written outside the HTTP surface; the lookup is also bound to the caller organization.

evidence.quote: No collection route exists, so INSERT is not HTTP-reachable.

releaseDisposition.blockingCondition: The defect blocks release as soon as any api_integrations row holding credentials exists in a production organization, whether written by an import, a migration or a future collection route, because from then on every member of that organization can read those credentials.
releaseDisposition.justification: The route returns stored credentials to the lowest role with no redaction, which would be release blocking on its own. It is held to a condition only because the application cannot create the rows, so the disclosure is empty until a row exists; the condition is concrete and the repair is a projection that omits the credentials.

defectRegister.title: A steward can change the apiEndpoint, the fieldMapping that maps Union Eyes member fields to the external HR or payroll system, the enabled flag and the sync frequency of an organization integration, while removing the same integration needs an administrator; the endpoint is accepted as any URL up to 2000 characters, the mapping as any JSON object, and the audit record names only the fields changed.

The extensions delete removes the api_integrations row outright, and integration_sync_logs references it with onDelete cascade, so deleting an integration silently erases its whole sync history (records processed, failed, errors, triggering user) while the audit record keeps only the integration id and name.

The extensions route reads, changes and deletes api_integrations rows under the name of an extension registry, but no route creates a row and nothing outside the route and the schema reads the table or its apiEndpoint, so enabling an integration, setting a sync frequency or repointing an endpoint is audited as integration.update and returns the updated row while no synchronization exists that the change could affect.

The event item read returns the whole calendar_events row to a steward or above, including meetingPassword, meetingUrl, agenda and attachments, whatever the row isPrivate and visibility columns say, because the generic factory and the route consult neither; below steward the only narrowing is memberId equal to the session user, so confidential events that name no member are unreachable to members and fully open to every steward.

The public event registration component fetches /api/events/{slug} without credentials and renders ticket price and free status, but the route requires an authenticated session at the member floor, compares the path value to the uuid primary key of calendar_events, and calendar_events has no slug, ticket price or free flag, so the public page can never load an event through it and a slug that is not a uuid reaches the database as a uuid comparison.

The occurrences route file is byte-identical to the event item route: its path value is the event id, and it reads, updates and deletes the calendar_events row itself, so a call that advertises one occurrence of a recurring event changes or removes the whole series row; recurrenceExceptions and parentEventId are never consulted, and the recurrence service that can add an exception or delete future instances is imported by no route.

The entitlement list returns every feature key whose org_entitlements status is active and ignores expiresAt and the backing contract, whereas the server-side entitlement check refuses an expired entitlement and verifies that the contract is active, so a client that gates premium features from this list shows a module as held after its entitlement has expired or its contract has ended.

The entitlement list answers 200 with an empty feature list for a caller whose organization cannot be resolved, which a client cannot tell from an organization that holds no entitlement, and it re-resolves the organization with getCurrentUser instead of using the organizationId its wrapper already placed in the context, reading org_entitlements through the shared db import with no tenant context.

The SSO provider list is open to every member and returns every column except the certificate and client secret, so any member reads the identity-provider entity ids, endpoints, OIDC client ids, the attribute mapping, the role mapping that says which directory groups become administrator or steward, the required groups, the metadata and the user id of the administrator who created each provider.

The SSO provider create casts the body to an interface and checks only that name, providerType and attributeMapping are present: providerType is any string although the schema comment allows saml and oidc, the entity id, SSO URL, issuer and certificate are not parsed or checked, the required fields of the chosen type are not required, there is no unique index on organization, entity id or issuer and no proof the organization owns the identity domain, requireGroups cannot be set, and autoProvision and enabled default to true.

No sign-in, token-exchange, provisioning or SCIM code reads sso_providers: the register route is the only reader and writer, so a provider an administrator registers with enabled and autoProvision true and an audit record of sso.provider.create never takes effect, and the decryption helper meant for the OIDC token exchange has no caller; the response reports a configured provider that nothing uses.

The register offers only a list and a create: no route changes, disables, rotates the secret of or deletes a provider, so a mistaken or compromised configuration can be corrected only by direct database work and the enabled flag set at creation cannot be turned off through the application.

The equity monitoring, self-identification and snapshot routes advertise the collection and statistics of special-category equity data but are the generic CRUD factory over member_segments, the saved member-search table: no self-identification answer, consent, statistic or snapshot is read, computed or stored, the dashboard receives a page of segment rows where it expects statistics and snapshots, and a create from the form or the generate-snapshot button lacks the name and filters the table requires.

The member-floor reads behind the equity paths return every member_segments row of the organization, including segments whose isPublic is false, because the table has no user or member owner column and the factory adds only the organization predicate, so any member reads the saved filter criteria (status, role, employer, worksite, bargaining unit, seniority) that stewards built privately.

The self-identification form puts a consent text before the member that promises encryption, aggregate-only reporting with a ten-member minimum, withdrawal and deletion at any time and seven-year retention, and then submits dataCollectionConsent true as a literal in the client body; the route stores no consent record, has no encryption, minimum cell size, withdrawal, deletion or retention behavior, and takes memberId and organizationId from the body that it ignores, so the assurances given at the point of consent are not implemented anywhere.

The self-identification create requires a steward, so the member the form is addressed to receives 403 on submit, while a steward or above is allowed to post a row on the member behalf with any body; a voluntary self-report that the union says is the member own choice is therefore reachable only by staff.

The only snapshot table, equity_snapshots in the financial-service schema, stores counts of Indigenous, visible-minority, disability and LGBTQ2+ members, executive-board and steward counts by group and average hourly pay by gender with no suppression flag, minimum group size or reader restriction, so a snapshot of a small board or worksite would publish counts that identify individuals; the table is revoked from the application roles today, which is why no route can reach it.

The incident item route reads at the member floor (readRole member) while the incident collection requires health_safety_rep, and the factory returns the whole workplace_incidents row: workplace_incidents has no userId, memberId, email or other column the low-role guard treats as personal (injuredPersonId and injuredPersonName are not on its list), so the guard stays open and any member of the organization who holds an incident id receives the injured person name, job title and employee id, body part, nature of injury, treatment, witness statements, investigation report, WSIB claim number and amount, photo and video links and the metadata JSON, with no audit of the read.

releaseDisposition.actualExposure: Any authenticated member of the organization who holds an incident id (the incident detail view requests it by id) receives the complete incident row including injury, treatment, witness and compensation fields from GET /api/health-safety/incidents/[id]; the list that would let a member discover ids is held to health_safety_rep, the by-id read is not.

potentialImpact.description: Health information about a named injured worker, witness statements and compensation claim details are disclosed to members who are neither the injured person, a health and safety representative nor an officer, with no read audit to show who saw them.

existingContainment.summary: The read is tenant scoped (the factory adds the organization predicate to the path-id lookup) and the incident id is a random uuid that the list, held to health_safety_rep, would otherwise expose; this limits the readers to members of the same organization who hold an id, not to the offices that should see injury data.

releaseDisposition.justification: The route answers 200 with the whole row to the lowest organization role, nothing in the handler or the table narrows the columns or the readers, and the harm is disclosure of health and compensation data of a named worker inside the organization; knowing an id is a weak barrier because ids travel in links and views, so the release is blocked until the by-id read is held to the same readers as the list and narrowed to the fields those readers need.
